Diastereodivergent Synthesis of b-Amino Alcohols by Dual-Metal-
Catalyzed Coupling of Alkoxyallenes with Aldimine Esters
Minghui Zhu+,Q inglong Zhang+,a nd Weiwei Zi*
Dedicated to the 70th anniversary of Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry (SIOC)
Abstract: Both syn- and anti-b-amino alcohols are common
structural motifs in natural products,d rug molecules,c hiral
ligands and catalysts.H owever,t he currently available methods
for synthesizing these motifs are limited to generate only one
diastereoisomer.T herefore,d evelopment of au nified method
for stereoselective access to complementary diastereomers
would be highly desirable.H erein, we report am ethod for
dual-metal-catalyzed diastereodivergent coupling of alkoxyal-
lenes with aldimine esters.B yc arefully selecting the two metals
and appropriate chiral ligands,w ec ould synthesize both syn-
and anti-b-amino alcohol motifs with high enantioselectivity
and diastereoselectivity from the same set of starting materials.
Furthermore,s tereodivergent syntheses of all four stereoiso-
mers of b-amino alcohols could be achieved. We demonstrated
the synthetic utility of this method by concisely synthesizing
two b-amino alcohol natural products,m ycestericins Fa nd G.
Introduction
b-Amino alcohol structural motifs are present in more
than 300,000 compounds,i ncluding > 2,000 natural products,
> 80 FDA-approved drugs and > 100 drug candidates.[1] b-
Amino alcohols are also important building blocks for chiral
ligands and auxiliaries used in asymmetric synthesis.[2] Com-
pounds with this moiety are conventionally prepared by
means of multistep transformations of a-amino acid deriva-
tives[3] or by stereoselective oxyamination of alkenes,[4] but
catalytic Csp3-Csp3 coupling reactions have emerged as
ap owerful alternative,o wing to their atom- and step-
economy.H owever, only af ew of the reported coupling
reactions are suitable for preparing b-amino alcohols with
vicinal stereocenters.[5,6 ] Fore xample,M alcolmson et al.
reported elegant reductive coupling reactions of azadienes
and ketones to access anti-b-amino tertiary alcohols.[5a]
Krische and co-workers enantioselectively synthesized anti-
b-amino alcohols by reductive coupling reactions of phthal-
imidoallenes and aldehydes,w hich proceed via ah ydrogen
auto-transfer process.[5b] Despite these achievements,n one of
the existing methods provide access to both syn-a nd anti-b-
amino alcohols.D iastereodivergent access to complementary
diastereomers of b-amino alcohols,e specially from the same
set of starting materials,w ould be highly desirable because
both syn-a nd anti-b-amino alcohols are useful for organic
synthesis.
Transition-metal-hydride-catalyzedc oupling reactions of
unsaturated hydrocarbons and enols or enolates has proven to
be ar eliable method for asymmetric construction of C@C
bonds.[7–9] In particular, alkoxyallenes can be used as coupling
partners for atom-economical preparation of chiral allylic
alcohol derivatives.[10] In pioneering work, Trost and co-
workers reported highly enantio- and diastereoselective
additions of azlactones and oxindoles to alkoxyallenes
(Scheme 1a ).[10a,b] More recently,J iang and co-workers de-
veloped ap rotocol for Pd-catalyzed or Brønsted acid
catalyzed addition reactions of pyrazolones and alkoxyallenes
with divergent regioselectivity.[10c] In these reactions,s ingle-
catalyst systems are employed, and the diastereoselectivity is
controlled by catalyst-substrate and substrate-substrate inter-
actions.T herefore,o nly the kinetically favored diastereoiso-
mer is accessible.S tereodivergent transition-metal-hydride-
catalyzed coupling reactions remain af ormidable chal-

lenge.[11] Rare examples include DongQsw ork on cooperative
Rh-H/amine-catalyzed coupling of aldehydes with alkynes[11a]
and our recent contribution involving synergistic Pd-H/Cu-
catalyzed coupling of 1,3-dienes with aldimine esters.[11b] In
these synergistic catalyst systems,[12] the two chiral catalysts
independently control the stereochemistry of the nucleophile
and electrophile during the coupling step;t herefore,s tereo-
divergent synthesis[13] can be achieved simply by choosing the
appropriate combination of catalyst chiralities.
Inspired by the aforementioned advances as well as the
recent achievements in stereodivergent allylic alkylation
reactions,[14–16] herein we report ap rotocol for dual-metal-
catalyzed diastereodivergent coupling of alkoxyallenes with
aldimine esters as an efficient method for preparing both syn-
and anti-b-amino alcohol motifs with high enantio- and
diastereoselectivities (Scheme 1b ). In addition, all four
stereoisomers of b-amino alcohols could be stereodivergently
synthesized simply by choosing the appropriate combination
of catalyst chiralities.N otably,a fter hydroxylation of the ester
group of the products to ac arboxylic acid, this method
provided as tereodivergent access to b-hydroxy a-amino
acids,w hich are one important type of unnatural a-amino
acids occasionally being observed in many bioactive natural
products.P revious works towards synthesis of these motifs
mainly relied on aldol type reactions,w hich could only obtain
one diastereisomer[17] and ab iocatalyisis pathway to access all
four stereoisomers were reported but it gave moderate
diastereoselectivities.[18] Therefore,t he dual-metal catalysis
strategy used herein showed huge superiority over the
traditional aldol reactions.F inally,a sa demonstration of this
method, we used the coupling reaction as ak ey step for the
total syntheses of two b-amino alcohol natural products,
mycestericins Fa nd G.
Results and Discussion
We began by investigating aC u/Pd catalyst system[11b,19, 20]
for the coupling of alkoxyallene 1a with aldimine ester 2a as
model substrates (Table 1). With (S,Sp)-Phosferrox L1 as the
chiral ligand for Cu, we tested the following bidentate chiral
ligands for Pd:( R,Sp)-Josiphos L4 and L5,( S,S)-Ph-BPE (L6),
(R)-tBu-PHOX( L7), (S)-BINAP (L8), (R)-Segphos L9 and
L10,a nd (S,S)-DACH-Ph Trost ligand (L11)( entries 1–8).
Although good to excellent enantioselectivities were ob-
tained, the diastereoselectivities were low,a si ndicated by the
3a a/4a a ratios.S creening of additional ligands revealed that
C2-symmetric bisphosphine ligands with phosphorus chirality
gave good stereocontrol. Fore xample,a 7:1 3a a/4a a ratio was
obtained by using (R,R,S,S)-DuanPhos (L12)a st he Pd ligand
(entry 9), and an even higher ratio was achieved with (S,S)-
QuinoxP (L13): anti-selective coupling product (2S,3S)-3a a
was obtained in 71 %i solated yield with > 99 % ee and 14:1
anti/syn selectivity (entry 10).
Next, we attempted to prepare the more challenging syn-
selective coupling product.[21] We first tested the combination
of L1-Cu with ent-L13-Pd (Table 1, entry 11). Although the
anti-coupling product did indeed predominate under these
conditions,t he syn/anti ratio was only moderate,a nd the yield
dropped to 64 %. We speculated that there may have been
strong noncovalent interactions between the Cu and Pd
catalysts during the coupling step and thus that mismatched

catalyst chirality may have led to the poor diastereoselectivity.
After exploring as eries of Pd and Cu catalyst combinations,
we discovered that syn-coupling to afford (2S,3R)-4a a
predominated when the same (S,Sp)-Phosferrox ligand was
used for both Pd and Cu (entries 12–14). Among the tested
ligands,p henyl-substituted (S,Sp)-Phosferrox (L3)g ave the
best syn/anti ratio (5.2:1, entry 14).
We hypothesized that because AgI has al arger ionic
radius than CuI,i ts complex with aldimine 1a would exhibit
greater structural flexibility,[22] which would help to reduce
ligand-ligand interference and improve control of the stereo-
chemistry.[23] To test this hypothesis,w ec arried out reactions
in which Cu(CH3CN)4PF6 was replaced with AgOAc,a nd we
were pleased to find that the L3-Ag/L3-Pd catalyst system
increased the syn/anti ratio to 12:1, although the yield was
slightly low (compare entries 14 and 15 in Table 1). In
attempts to improve both the selectivity and the yield, we
investigated various solvents (entries 16–19). Theb est reac-
tion medium was cyclopentyl methyl ether,w hich gave an
80 %y ield of syn-selective coupling product (2S,3R)-4a a with
> 99 % ee and 18:1 syn/anti selectivity (entry 19). They ield
and syn/anti ratio were improved further by using as light
excess of AgOAc (entry 20 vs.e ntry 19).[24] Notably,t he
regioselectivities of both the Pd/Cu- and Pd/Ag-catalyzed
reactions were completely controlled.[13c] As ac ontrol experi-
ment, without Cu or Ag catalyst, only utilizing Pd catalyst did
not catalyze the reaction (entries 21 and 22 ).
Having developed conditions for diastereodivergent cou-
pling of alkoxyallenes with aldimine esters,w ee xplored the
substrate scope of the reactions,s tarting with the Cu/Pd-
catalyzed anti-s elective coupling (Table 2). Alkoxyallenes
1 with various R1 groups were well tolerated in reactions with
aldimine ester 2a .F or example,w hen R1 was a para-
methoxybenzyl, meta-fluorobenzyl, 2-naphthalenemethyl, 2-
indanyl, or phenyl group,c orresponding products (2S,3S)-
3a b-3a f were obtained in good yields (54–77 %) with good
diastereoselectivities (10:1–16:1) and excellent enantioselec-
tivities (96– > 99 % ee). When R1 was an alkyl group
(cyclohexyl, n-octyl, or 3-phenylpropyl), the reaction smooth-
ly gave desired products 3a g–3a i with good stereoselectivi-
ties.I na ddition, sterically hindered alkyl alkoxyallenes also
underwent the reaction, as demonstrated by the formation of
coupling products 3a j and 3a k.A lkoxyallenes derived from
the natural products (S)-prolinol, (S)-citronellol, phytol,
geraniol, and cholesterol were subjected to the coupling
reaction, and found to afford anti-b-amino alcohol derivatives
3a l–3a p,r espectively,i nh igh yields with good diastereose-
lectivities.W hen the R2 group of the aldimine ester was
changed from methyl to ethyl, n-propyl, or n-butyl, slightly
lower yields were obtained (3b a–3d a). Similarly,c hanging the
methyl ester to the more bulky i-propyl ester also decreased
the yield (3e a). These results imply that the reaction was
sensitive to the steric bulk of the aldimine ester.H owever,
cyclic aldimine esters were well tolerated, giving good yields
of products containing ac yclic imine (3f a), al actone (3g a),
and an oxazoline moiety (3h a)w ith high diastereo- and
enantioselectivities.A thioether group was also compatible
with the reaction conditions,a ss hown by the formation of 3i a,
which was obtained in 62 %y ield with 16:1 dr and > 99 % ee.
Ak etamine derived from ag lycine ester underwent the
reaction, giving 3j a in 56 %y ield with > 99 % ee,a lbeit with
ap oor dr. Thes tereochemistry of 3h a was determined by
single-crystal X-ray diffraction and the absolute configuration
was assigned to (2S,3S).[25]
We next examined the scope of the Ag/Pd-catalyzed syn-
selective coupling reaction (Table 3). Av ariety of benzyl- and
alkyl-substituted alkoxyallenes 1 reacted with 2a to give the
desired anti-coupling products (4a b–4 ah)i ng ood yields with
high diastereoselectivities and excellent enantioselectivities.
Natural-product-derived alkoxyallenes also showed good
reactivities,a ffording good yields of syn-b-amino alcohol
derivatives 4a i–4 al.C hiral alkoxyallenes derived from (R)-
and (S)-1-phenylethanol reacted with 2a to give (2S,3R,R)-
4a m and (2S,3R,S)-4a n,r espectively.T he existing chiral
centers in these substrates had little influence on the
stereochemistry of the newly formed stereocenters (4a m vs.
4a n). All the aldimine esters shown in the lower panel of
Table 2w ere also tested in the Ag/Pd system, and as expected,
the corresponding syn-coupling products were formed exclu-
sively as the main isomer,i ny ields ranging from 40 to 85 %. In
all these examples,t he diastereoselectivities were well
controlled (dr = 7:1–20:1), except in the case of the reaction
of ag lycine-ester-derived ketamine (4j a), for which the dr
was only 2:1. Note also that the enantioselectivity of the Ag/
Pd-catalyzed reaction of the methionine-derived aldimine
ester was lower than that of the Cu/Pd-catalyzed reaction of
the same substrate (80 %f or 4i a vs. > 99 %f or 3i a).
To demonstrate the stereodivergence of this reaction, we
coupled 1a with 2a with catalysis by four separate catalyst
systems: L13-Pd/L1-Cu, ent-L13-Pd/ent-L1-Cu, L3-Pd/L3-Ag,
and ent-L3-Pd/ent-L3-Ag (Scheme 2). In this way,w ew ere
able to obtain all four stereoisomers of the coupling product-
(2S,3S)-3a a,( 2R,3R)-3a a,( 2R,3S)-4a a,a nd (2S,3R)-4a a-in
optically pure form (> 99 % ee)w ith dr values of + 14:1.
Considerable success in the stereodivergent synthesis of
compounds with vicinal stereocenters has been achieved.[13–15]
however, stereodivergent preparation of compounds with
more than two stereocenters has not yet been reported.
Herein, to further demonstrate the robustness of our dual-
catalyst systems,w ec arried out stereodivergent syntheses of
amino alcohol derivatives with three stereocenters by means
of coupling reactions of alkoxyallenes (S)- and (R)-1x with
aldimine ester 2a (Scheme 3). With appropriate combinations

To further demonstrate the utility of this stereodivergent
coupling method, we used it for total syntheses of two amino
alcohol natural products,m ycestericins Fa nd G
(Scheme 6).[29] First, we carried out as caled-up coupling
reaction of para-methoxybenzyl-protected alkoxyallene 1a
and oxazoline 2h by using the L13-Pd/L1-Cu system, which
afforded corresponding anti-coupling product (2S,3S)-3h a in
60 %y ield with 99 % ee and 6:1d r. Removal the protecting
group afforded alcohol 6a ,w hich was subjected to an olefin
metathesis reaction with ketoalkene 7 and Hoveyda-Grubbs
II catalyst to give 8a in 65 %y ield. Hydrogenation of the
double bond and hydroxylation of the oxazoline ring and
ester group completed the total synthesis of mycestericin F.
Using as imilar route,b ut starting from syn-coupling product
(2S,3R)-3h b obtained with the L3-Pd/L3-Ag catalyst system,
we also achieved at otal synthesis of mycestericin G. The
spectra of the synthetic samples were identical to the reported
spectra.[30]
Conclusion
In summary,w eh ave developed ap rotocol for diaste-
reodivergent coupling of alkoxyallenes with aldimine esters.
By choosing the appropriate dual-metal catalyst system (Pd/
Cu or Pd/Ag) and appropriate chiral ligands,w ec ould
synthesize both anti-a nd syn-b-amino alcohol motifs with
high enantioselectivity and diastereoselectivity from the same
set of starting materials.T hese mild reactions have ab road
substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance.T he
coupling products could be further manipulated to access
various useful synthons.S tereodivergent syntheses of all four
stereoisomers of b-amino alcohols with vicinal stereocenters
were achieved simply by varying the configurations of the two
chiral metal catalysts.U sing this coupling reaction as the key
step,w ea ccomplished total syntheses of natural products
mycestericin Fa nd G.
